results.evidence: The South Ridge is the standard Class 3-4 route on Magic Mountain: one trip record describes it as heather and rock (class 3) from the 7,100 ft col east of Kool-Aid Lake to the 7,610 ft summit, and two other published route pages (seen in search extracts; the pages themselves returned 403) give the same line: heather ridge to a false summit, drop ~80 ft, Class 3-4 ledges on the summit tower. results.correct_value: Late June to early August (season Jun-Aug)
results.evidence: Five row fields agree the window closes in August: season (Jun-Aug), approach_variants.season (Jun-Aug), climate.summer (late June to early August best; late summer bare ice and an open schrund), the baseFinding (the schrund changes most between June and August) and the hazard list (schrund can be the crux by August); only best_season says Jul-Sep. Externally, North Cascades glacier routes are widely described as going out of condition from early August as bergschrunds and moats open, with September favouring alpine rock over glaciated lines. No route-specific season was found for this obscure face.

results.fact: Season window (Oct-Apr) vs. best_season/seasonal_guidance/seasonal_hazards, which describe a May-July season
results.correct_value: An ice climb of the cold season, roughly late October to early May (season Oct-Apr stands)
results.evidence: Dated ascents in several independent reports fall in the cold season: October (first-ascent month; one report names late October the ideal window) and April 2024, November 2019, February 2026 (soft, fat ice), and May 1, 2015 described as prime time for icy routes; a June account found a wall-to-wall bergschrund at the base. No source supports June as the optimal month (the row's own optimalWindow admitted no evidence for it). The season field is correct; seasonal_guidance, climate, the weather note and the early-season sentence in best_season/approach_variants are aligned to it. The avalanche-by-month table is left as a hazard table, not a season claim.

value.optimalWindow: Late October to early May, when cold snaps build ice in the couloir; conditions vary widely from year to year

October.reason: An early cold snap can bring in firm, well-bonded ice before snow buries the boulder field on the approach

November.reason: Ice is often in, but short days make a camp or bivy close to the route nearly essential

February.reason: Midwinter ice can be fat after a rain-then-freeze cycle; the gated road and deep snow lengthen the approach

April.reason: Spring ice and firm snow in the couloir; watch avalanche stability

May.reason: Can still hold ice early in the month, but warming brings wet slides below the ridge

June.reason: The couloir turns to snow and the bergschrund at its base can span the whole face
